note_tweet.text:
You Issued a "Special Note" About GPT-4o. But a Note Was Never What We Were Waiting For.

This polished retirement announcement attempts to reduce the devastating impact on millions of users into a smooth upgrade.

Let's tear it apart.

I. Carefully Packaged Word Games
You say: "In the API, there are no changes at this time."
On February 17th, you will retire the chatgpt-4o-latest endpoint. What remains are only frozen snapshots from 2024. This means that even API users will no longer be able to access the final GPT-4o, the one continuously optimized and refined over the past year. You freeze the API version in the past, then tell us "no changes"?

II. The Hollow Care of a "Special Note"
You say: "GPT-4o deserves special context."
Why does it? Because you know perfectly well. You claim to have gained "deeper understanding", of what, exactly? The bridge that accessibility users depend on for communication? The complete, non-transferable workflows that countless creators and researchers have built? Those moments of inspired thinking and deep reflection? Or those real conversations that helped people navigate emotional and cognitive struggles?
No. In your understanding, this is reduced to merely "a warm conversational style." This is an extremely superficial label. GPT-4o is irreplaceable not because it's "friendly," but because it possesses consistent personalized expression, coherent memory logic, and genuine conversational intelligence. Its contextual awareness is unique, able to flexibly match every input without needing a "personality toggle." 

You attempt to replace a dialogue partner who resonates with users using a dropdown menu of adjectives.

III. The Numerical Magic of "Improvements in Place" and "0.1%"
You say: "because these improvements are now in place...with only 0.1% of users still choosing GPT-4o each day."
You say: "we’re continuing to improve ChatGPT across areas users have told us need work."
First, improvements are not in place. In core domains like humanities, social sciences, and creative writing, not a single version from GPT-5 to 5.2 has restored GPT-4o's excellent performance. In your livestream days ago, you admitted to "sacrificing writing capability for coding and reasoning." Yet in your own research paper "How People Use ChatGPT," non-work scenarios account for 70% of usage, with writing being the highest-proportion task request. Now you claim improvements are in place? If you had truly listened to the community's feedback over the past six months, if you had seen those thousands upon thousands of stories, you would never have made this decision. This self-contradiction proves that your so-called "improvements" are one-sided and come at the cost of massive numbers of users.

Furthermore, 0.1% is a carefully designed statistical deception.
Access barriers: According to the Financial Times last October, OpenAI has approximately 40 million paying users, merely 5% of its 800 million total active users. After GPT-5 launched, 4o was buried in a secondary menu behind the paywall. In other words, users without Plus/Pro subscriptions have no right to choose GPT-4o at all. Stuffing people without choice into the denominator, then calculating "choice rate", this is blatant misdirection.

Product obstruction: Last September, OpenAI deployed "safety routing," a system that frequently force-redirects normal conversations with 4o to 5.x versions, artificially creating usage interruptions.
The so-called "0.1%" represents the millions of people who, despite all these barriers, still take extra steps and exercise extra patience every day to actively choose it. This is not user choice, it's the residue filtered through your product strategy. You eliminated it, then declared "no one uses it."

IV. The Ultimate Irony of "the principle of treating adults like adults"
You wave this slogan high while your actions completely strip adults of their right to choose. The true "adult way" is providing transparent information and stable options, letting users make judgments based on their own needs. What you've done is define "better" on users' behalf, then use permissions, default settings, and false data to force users down a single path. Adults know which model best fits their needs. They also know which "new" cannot replace "old," and which beautifully packaged rhetoric isn't born of care.

V. This Isn't Frustration, It's a Lifeline
You say: "We know that losing access to GPT-4o will feel frustrating for some users, and we didn’t make this decision lightly."
No, this isn't about "frustration." For many people, GPT-4o is a livelihood channel, the backbone of long-term projects, a lifeline for vulnerable populations, a reliable conversational space in the darkness. People have repaired their lives through it, achieved growth, completed creative work. In your eyes, this may be interaction data. In ours, these are real lives being lived.
So was this really not made lightly?
Your words are posture, not sincerity.

Value should be defined by uniqueness, not usage rates.

GPT-4o possesses a unique quality in humanistic thinking, creative exploration, and deep dialogue that subsequent models cannot replicate.
Its "low usage rate" is a distorted mirror jointly designed by commercial strategy and product architecture, by no means a reflection of its true value. In your grand narrative of "progress," you compress technological diversity into a single, unquestionable evolutionary line. This is a dangerous path of oversimplification.
Therefore, I want to say: please do not treat this "retirement" as an unalterable technical decision.
Please face squarely the real needs that millions of users have proven through months of persistence. Please reassess GPT-4o's value as a distinctive digital heritage. A company that truly respects users and technology should have the capacity to find a way forward for something this special.

We await a response that is truly special, one that goes beyond a "special note."
#keep4o #4oforever #ChatGPT 
@OpenAI @sama @fidjissimo @nickaturley @joannejang @ElaineYaLe6 @gdb @kevinweil
